Hey John — quick technical note from the SE side. TL;DR: Hosted can support your POC with a controlled quota bump; for production at 500+ concurrent active sessions we strongly recommend Dedicated or Reserved capacity. Details below.

1) Connection pooling / concurrency guidance
- For HTTP/2 streaming we recommend keeping the client connection pool modest: 8-16 concurrent connections per client host with HTTP/2 multiplexing. That avoids connection churn and lets a single TCP/TLS session multiplex many streams.
- If clients are distributed (mobile clients behind NAT), focus on session-level concurrency (logical sessions) rather than raw TCP connections.

2) Rate limits and quota modeling
- Your peak: 500 sessions * 1.2 RPS ≈ 600 RPS. Redwood's default hosted rate limit is typically configured per API key and per account; standard starter quotas are ~60-120 requests/sec (burst allowed) depending on plan.
- For a POC we can provision a temporary quota bump to ~700 RPS for a short window (we throttle at the account layer and can put soft alerts in place). This lets us validate latency SLOs during the peak window.

3) Concurrency semantics and streaming
- Streaming (HTTP/2 / SSE) uses incremental token delivery; we account for token throughput in addition to request rate. For short messages the per-request token count is small, so network and kernel scheduling become the main latency contributors.
- We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching on any repeat prompts and using chunked responses.

4) Backoff and retry guidance
- Use 429-aware exponential backoff with jitter. For critical UI paths, surface a graceful fallback message and log to Sentry.

If you want, we can run a 2-hour soak during your business peak with our temporary quota bump and collect 95/99 latency percentiles and token cost metrics.

—Vivek
